<td class="text"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">2.</span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0.25in;"/><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"> Miscellaneous Financial Information</span><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">Crude oil, products and merchandise inventories are carried at the lower of current market value or cost, generally determined under the last-in first-out method (LIFO).</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"> The Corporation&#8217;s results for the first quarter of 2020 include a before-tax charge of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">2,777 million, included in &#8220;Crude oil and product purchases&#8221; on the Statement of Income, from writing down the book value of inventories to their market value at the end of the period. At year-end, any required adjustment is considered permanent and is incorporated into the LIFO carrying value of the inventory.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 6.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 6.00pt; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The COVID-19 pandemic resulted in substantial reductions in demand for crude oil, natural gas, and petroleum products. This reduction in demand led to sharp declines in industry prices and considerable volatility in financial markets during the quarter. Based on deteriorating industry conditions and a significant reduction in its market capitalization, the Corporation assessed its goodwill balances and certain asset groups for impairment and recognized after-tax impairment charges of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">787 million. These charges included goodwill impairment of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">562 million in Upstream, Downstream, and Chemical reporting units and other impairment charges of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">225 million, mainly in the Upstream segment. For the goodwill impairment charges, the fair values of the impacted reporting units primarily reflected market-based estimates of historical EBITDA multiples at the end of the quarter. For the other impairment charges, which mainly relate to the Corporation&#8217;s investment in an Upstream equity company, recent third party price outlooks, internal estimates of future volumes and costs, and estimates of discount rates for similar properties were used to estimate fair value. The charges related to goodwill impairment are included in &#8220;Depreciation and depletion&#8221; on the Statement of Income while the charges related to other impairments are largely included in &#8220;Income from equity affiliates.&#8221;</span></p><span></span>

<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Allowance for Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL)<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">3 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2020</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AllowanceForCreditLossAbstract', window );"><strong>Allowance For Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL) [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AllowanceForCreditLossesTextBlock', window );">Allowance For Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL)</a></td>
<td class="text"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">10.</span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0.25in;"/><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">Allowance for Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL)</span><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">Effective January 1, 2020, the Corporation adopted the Financial Accounting Standards Board&#8217;s update, </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-style: italic; font-size: 10.00pt">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326)</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">, as amended. The standard requires a valuation allowance for credit losses be recognized for certain financial assets that reflects the current expected credit loss over the asset&#8217;s contractual life. The valuation allowance considers the risk of loss, even if remote, and considers past events, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. The standard requires this expected loss methodology for trade receivables, certain other financial assets and off-balance sheet credit exposures. The cumulative effect adjustment related to the adoption of this standard reduced equity by $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">93 million.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation is exposed to credit losses primarily through sales of petroleum products, crude oil, NGLs and natural gas, as well as loans to equity companies and joint venture receivables. A counterparty&#8217;s ability to pay is assessed through a credit review process that considers payment terms, the counterparty&#8217;s established credit rating or the Corporation&#8217;s assessment of the counterparty&#8217;s credit worthiness, contract terms, country of operation, and other risks. The Corporation can require prepayment or collateral to mitigate certain credit risks.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation groups financial assets into portfolios that share similar risk characteristics for purposes of determining the allowance for credit losses. Each reporting period, the Corporation assesses whether a significant change in the risk of credit loss has occurred. Among the quantitative and qualitative factors considered are historical financial data, current conditions, industry and country risk, current credit ratings and the quality of third-party guarantees secured from the counterparty. Financial assets are written off in whole, or in part, when practical recovery efforts have been exhausted and no reasonable expectation of recovery exists. Subsequent recoveries of amounts previously written off are recognized in earnings. The Corporation manages receivable portfolios using past due balances as a key credit quality indicator. </span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; line-height: 115.00%; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation recognizes a credit allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures as a liability on the balance sheet, separate from the allowance for credit losses related to recognized financial assets.</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"> Among these exposures are unfunded loans to equity companies and financial guarantees that cannot be cancelled unilaterally by the Corporation.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; line-height: 115.00%; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; line-height: 115.00%; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">During the first quarter of 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic spread rapidly through most areas of the world resulting in economic uncertainty, global financial market volatility, and negative effects in the credit markets. The Corporation has considered these effects, along with the significantly lower balances of trade receivables at the end of the quarter, in its estimate of credit losses and concluded no material adjustment to credit allowances in the quarter was required. At March 31, 2020, the Corporation&#8217;s evaluation of financial assets under </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-style: italic; font-size: 10.00pt">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326)</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">, as amended, included $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">17,740 million of notes and accounts receivable, net of allowances of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">148 million, and $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">9,211 million of loans and long-term receivables, net of allowances of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">441 million, and certain other financial assets where there is immaterial risk of loss.</span></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: none; margin-bottom: 0.001pt; width: 100%; margin-left: 0.00pt"><tr style="height: 0.08in"><td style="vertical-align: bottom; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: bottom; <td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_InventoryPolicyTextBlock', window );">Inventory Policy</a></td>
<td class="text"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">Crude oil, products and merchandise inventories are carried at the lower of current market value or cost, generally determined under the last-in first-out method (LIFO).</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The earnings impact may be adjusted upward or downward this year based on prevailing market prices at the time of future evaluations. At year-end, any required adjustment is considered permanent and is incorporated into the LIFO carrying value of the inventory.</span><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_LegalCostsPolicyTextBlock', window );">Legal Costs Policy</a></td>
<td class="text"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation accrues an undiscounted liability for those contingencies where the incurrence of a loss is probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If a range of amounts can be reasonably estimated and no amount within the range is a better estimate than any other amount, then the minimum of the range is accrued. The Corporation does not record liabilities when the likelihood that the liability has been incurred is probable but the amount cannot be reasonably estimated or when the liability is believed to be only reasonably possible or remote. For contingencies where an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible and which are significant, the Corporation discloses the nature of the contingency and, where feasible, an estimate of the possible loss. For purposes of our contingency disclosures, &#8220;significant&#8221; includes material matters, as well as other matters which management believes should be disclosed.</span><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock', window );">Credit Loss Financial Instrument Policy</a></td>
<td class="text"><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation groups financial assets into portfolios that share similar risk characteristics for purposes of determining the allowance for credit losses. Each reporting period, the Corporation assesses whether a significant change in the risk of credit loss has occurred. Among the quantitative and qualitative factors considered are historical financial data, current conditions, industry and country risk, current credit ratings and the quality of third-party guarantees secured from the counterparty. Financial assets are written off in whole, or in part, when practical recovery efforts have been exhausted and no reasonable expectation of recovery exists. Subsequent recoveries of amounts previously written off are recognized in earnings. The Corporation manages receivable portfolios using past due balances as a key credit quality indicator. </span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation recognizes a credit allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures as a liability on the balance sheet, separate from the allowance for credit losses related to recognized financial assets.</span><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

In addition, the Corporation uses commodity-based contracts, including derivatives, to manage commodity price risk and for trading purposes. Commodity contracts held for trading purposes are presented in the Consolidated Statement of Income on a net basis in the line &#8220;Sales and other operating revenue.&#8221; The Corporation&#8217;s commodity derivatives are not accounted for under hedge accounting. At times, the Corporation also enters into currency and interest rate derivatives, none of which are material to the Corporation&#8217;s financial position as of March 31, 2020, and December 31, 2019, or results of operations for the periods ended March 31, 2020 and 2019.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">Credit risk associated with the Corporation&#8217;s derivative position is mitigated by several factors, including the use of derivative clearing exchanges and the quality of and financial limits placed on derivative counterparties. <td class="text"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">3.</span><span style="display: inline-block; width: 0.25in;"/><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">Litigation and Other Contingencies</span><p style="margin-top: 6.00pt; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">Litigation</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 6.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">A variety of claims have been made against ExxonMobil and certain of its consolidated subsidiaries in a number of pending lawsuits. Management has regular litigation reviews, including updates from corporate and outside counsel, to assess the need for accounting recognition or disclosure of these contingencies. </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation accrues an undiscounted liability for those contingencies where the incurrence of a loss is probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If a range of amounts can be reasonably estimated and no amount within the range is a better estimate than any other amount, then the minimum of the range is accrued. The Corporation does not record liabilities when the likelihood that the liability has been incurred is probable but the amount cannot be reasonably estimated or when the liability is believed to be only reasonably possible or remote. For contingencies where an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible and which are significant, the Corporation discloses the nature of the contingency and, where feasible, an estimate of the possible loss. For purposes of our contingency disclosures, &#8220;significant&#8221; includes material matters, as well as other matters which management believes should be disclosed.</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"> ExxonMobil will continue to defend itself vigorously in these matters. Based on a consideration of all relevant facts and circumstances, the Corporation does not believe the ultimate outcome of any currently pending lawsuit against ExxonMobil will have a material adverse effect upon the Corporation's operations, financial condition, or financial statements taken as a whole.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 6.00pt; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt">Other Contingencies</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 6.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The Corporation and certain of its consolidated subsidiaries were contingently liable at March 31, 2020, for guarantees relating to notes, loans and performance under contracts. Where guarantees for environmental remediation and other similar matters do not include a stated cap, the amounts reflect management&#8217;s estimate of the maximum potential exposure. These guarantees are not reasonably likely to have a material effect on the Corporation&#8217;s financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources.</span></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 11%; border-top: solid #000000 1pt; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0; text-align: right"><p style="margin-bottom: 0; text-align: right"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 9.00pt">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 8%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0; text-align: center"><p style="margin-bottom: 0; text-align: center"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td></tr><tr style="height: 0.07in"><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 4%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 4%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-style: italic; font-size: 10.00pt"> (1) </span></p></td><td colspan="2" style="vertical-align: middle; width: 38%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-style: italic; font-size: 10.00pt">ExxonMobil share</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 11%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0; text-align: right"><p style="margin-bottom: 0; text-align: right"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0; text-align: center"><p style="margin-bottom: 0; text-align: center"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 11%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0; text-align: right"><p style="margin-bottom: 0; text-align: right"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 2%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0"><p style="margin-bottom: 0"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 9.00pt">&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 8%; padding-top: 0; padding-right: 0; padding-bottom: 0; padding-left: 0; text-align: center"><p style="margin-bottom: 0; text-align: center"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'">&#160;</span></p></td></tr></table><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">Additionally, the Corporation and its affiliates have numerous long-term sales and purchase commitments in their various business activities, all of which are expected to be fulfilled with no adverse consequences material to the Corporation&#8217;s operations or financial condition.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 8.00pt; text-align: justify"><span style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the world have been, and may in the future be, affected from time to time in varying degree by political developments and laws and regulations, such as forced divestiture of assets; restrictions on production, imports and exports; price controls; tax increases and retroactive tax claims; expropriation of property; cancellation of contract rights and environmental regulations. Both the likelihood of such occurrences and their overall effect upon the Corporation vary greatly from country to country and are not predictable.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">In accordance with a Venezuelan nationalization decree issued in February 2007, a subsidiary of the Venezuelan National Oil Company (PdVSA) assumed the operatorship of the Cerro Negro Heavy Oil Project. The decree also required conversion of the Cerro Negro Project into a &#8220;mixed enterprise&#8221; and an increase in PdVSA&#8217;s or one of its affiliate&#8217;s ownership interest in the Project. ExxonMobil refused to accede to the terms proffered by the government, and on June 27, 2007, the government expropriated ExxonMobil&#8217;s </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">41.67 percent interest in the Cerro Negro Project.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">ExxonMobil collected awards of $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">908 million in an arbitration against PdVSA under the rules of the International Chamber of Commerce in respect of an indemnity related to the Cerro Negro Project and $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">260 million in an arbitration for compensation due for the La Ceiba Project and for export curtailments at the Cerro Negro Project under rules of International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID). An ICSID arbitration award relating to the Cerro Negro Project&#8217;s expropriation ($</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">1.4 billion) was annulled based on a determination that a prior Tribunal failed to adequately explain why the cap on damages in the indemnity owed by PdVSA did not affect or limit the amount owed for the expropriation of the Cerro Negro Project. ExxonMobil filed a new claim seeking to restore the original award of damages for the Cerro Negro Project with ICSID on September 26, 2018.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">The net impact of this matter on the Corporation&#8217;s consolidated financial results cannot be reasonably estimated. Regardless, the Corporation does not expect the resolution to have a material effect upon the Corporation&#8217;s operations or financial condition.</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">An affiliate of ExxonMobil is one of the Contractors under a Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) covering the Erha block located in the offshore waters of Nigeria. ExxonMobil's affiliate is the operator of the block and owns a </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">56.25 percent interest under the PSC. The Contractors are in dispute with NNPC regarding NNPC's lifting of crude oil in excess of its entitlement under the terms of the PSC. In accordance with the terms of the PSC, the Contractors initiated arbitration in Abuja, Nigeria, under the Nigerian Arbitration and Conciliation Act. On October 24, 2011, a three-member arbitral Tribunal issued an award upholding the Contractors' position in all material respects and awarding damages to the Contractors jointly in an amount of approximately $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">1.8 billion plus $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt">234 million in accrued interest. The Contractors petitioned a Nigerian federal court for enforcement of the award, and NNPC petitioned the same court to have the award set aside. On May 22, 2012, the court set aside the award. The Contractors appealed that judgment to the Court of Appeal, Abuja Judicial Division. On July 22, 2016, the Court of Appeal upheld the decision of the lower court setting aside the award. On October 21, 2016, the Contractors appealed the decision to the Supreme Court of Nigeria. In June 2013, the Contractors filed a lawsuit against NNPC in the Nigerian federal high court in order to preserve their ability to seek enforcement of the PSC in the courts if necessary. Following dismissal by this court, the Contractors appealed to the Nigerian Court of Appeal in June 2016. In October 2014, the Contractors filed suit in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York (SDNY) to enforce, if necessary, the arbitration award against NNPC assets residing within that jurisdiction. NNPC moved to dismiss the lawsuit. On September 4, 2019, the SDNY dismissed the Contractors&#8217; petition to recognize and enforce the Erha arbitration award. The Contractors filed a notice of appeal in the Second Circuit on October 2, 2019. At this time, the net impact of this matter on the Corporation's consolidated financial results cannot be reasonably estimated. However, regardless of the outcome of enforcement proceedings, the Corporation does not expect the proceedings to have a material effect upon the Corporation's operations or financial condition.</span></p><span></span>
</td>

    <us-gaap:AdditionalFinancialInformationDisclosureTextBlock
      contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2020_TO_Mar31_2020_Entity_0000034088"
      id="ID_21e7c3351476497f8c353d60f2f9e4e5">&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;2.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="display: inline-block; width: 0.25in;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt; Miscellaneous Financial Information&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Crude oil, products and merchandise inventories are carried at the lower of current market value or cost, generally determined under the last-in first-out method (LIFO).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt; The Corporation&#x2019;s results for the first quarter of 2020 include a before-tax charge of $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;2,777 million, included in &#x201c;Crude oil and product purchases&#x201d; on the Statement of Income, from writing down the book value of inventories to their market value at the end of the period. This adjustment, together with a similar adjustment for equity companies included in &#x201c;Income from equity affiliates,&#x201d; resulted in a $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;2,096 million after-tax charge to earnings (excluding noncontrolling interests) and will be re-evaluated at the end of each quarter in 2020. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The earnings impact may be adjusted upward or downward this year based on prevailing market prices at the time of future evaluations. At year-end, any required adjustment is considered permanent and is incorporated into the LIFO carrying value of the inventory.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 6.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 6.00pt; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The COVID-19 pandemic resulted in substantial reductions in demand for crude oil, natural gas, and petroleum products. This reduction in demand led to sharp declines in industry prices and considerable volatility in financial markets during the quarter. Based on deteriorating industry conditions and a significant reduction in its market capitalization, the Corporation assessed its goodwill balances and certain asset groups for impairment and recognized after-tax impairment charges of $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;787 million. These charges included goodwill impairment of $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;562 million in Upstream, Downstream, and Chemical reporting units and other impairment charges of $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;225 million, mainly in the Upstream segment. For the goodwill impairment charges, the fair values of the impacted reporting units primarily reflected market-based estimates of historical EBITDA multiples at the end of the quarter. For the other impairment charges, which mainly relate to the Corporation&#x2019;s investment in an Upstream equity company, recent third party price outlooks, internal estimates of future volumes and costs, and estimates of discount rates for similar properties were used to estimate fair value. The charges related to goodwill impairment are included in &#x201c;Depreciation and depletion&#x201d; on the Statement of Income while the charges related to other impairments are largely included in &#x201c;Income from equity affiliates.&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:AdditionalFinancialInformationDisclosureTextBlock>

    <us-gaap:LegalMattersAndContingenciesTextBlock
      contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2020_TO_Mar31_2020_Entity_0000034088"
      id="ID_6b4c4fbcd5e648b889d403d5a479f606">&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;3.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="display: inline-block; width: 0.25in;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Litigation and Other Contingencies&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 6.00pt; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Litigation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 6.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;A variety of claims have been made against ExxonMobil and certain of its consolidated subsidiaries in a number of pending lawsuits. Management has regular litigation reviews, including updates from corporate and outside counsel, to assess the need for accounting recognition or disclosure of these contingencies. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation accrues an undiscounted liability for those contingencies where the incurrence of a loss is probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If a range of amounts can be reasonably estimated and no amount within the range is a better estimate than any other amount, then the minimum of the range is accrued. The Corporation does not record liabilities when the likelihood that the liability has been incurred is probable but the amount cannot be reasonably estimated or when the liability is believed to be only reasonably possible or remote. For contingencies where an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible and which are significant, the Corporation discloses the nature of the contingency and, where feasible, an estimate of the possible loss. For purposes of our contingency disclosures, &#x201c;significant&#x201d; includes material matters, as well as other matters which management believes should be disclosed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt; ExxonMobil will continue to defend itself vigorously in these matters. Based on a consideration of all relevant facts and circumstances, the Corporation does not believe the ultimate outcome of any currently pending lawsuit against ExxonMobil will have a material adverse effect upon the Corporation's operations, financial condition, or financial statements taken as a whole.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 6.00pt; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Other Contingencies&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 6.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation and certain of its consolidated subsidiaries were contingently liable at March 31, 2020, for guarantees relating to notes, loans and performance under contracts. Where guarantees for environmental remediation and other similar matters do not include a stated cap, the amounts reflect management&#x2019;s estimate of the maximum potential exposure. These guarantees are not reasonably likely to have a material effect on the Corporation&#x2019;s financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; restrictions on production, imports and exports; price controls; tax increases and retroactive tax claims; expropriation of property; cancellation of contract rights and environmental regulations. Both the likelihood of such occurrences and their overall effect upon the Corporation vary greatly from country to country and are not predictable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;In accordance with a Venezuelan nationalization decree issued in February 2007, a subsidiary of the Venezuelan National Oil Company (PdVSA) assumed the operatorship of the Cerro Negro Heavy Oil Project. The decree also required conversion of the Cerro Negro Project into a &#x201c;mixed enterprise&#x201d; and an increase in PdVSA&#x2019;s or one of its affiliate&#x2019;s ownership interest in the Project. ExxonMobil refused to accede to the terms proffered by the government, and on June 27, 2007, the government expropriated ExxonMobil&#x2019;s &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;41.67 percent interest in the Cerro Negro Project.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;ExxonMobil collected awards of $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;908 million in an arbitration against PdVSA under the rules of the International Chamber of Commerce in respect of an indemnity related to the Cerro Negro Project and $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;260 million in an arbitration for compensation due for the La Ceiba Project and for export curtailments at the Cerro Negro Project under rules of International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID). An ICSID arbitration award relating to the Cerro Negro Project&#x2019;s expropriation ($&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;1.4 billion) was annulled based on a determination that a prior Tribunal failed to adequately explain why the cap on damages in the indemnity owed by PdVSA did not affect or limit the amount owed for the expropriation of the Cerro Negro Project. ExxonMobil filed a new claim seeking to restore the original award of damages for the Cerro Negro Project with ICSID on September 26, 2018.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The net impact of this matter on the Corporation&#x2019;s consolidated financial results cannot be reasonably estimated. Regardless, the Corporation does not expect the resolution to have a material effect upon the Corporation&#x2019;s operations or financial condition.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;An affiliate of ExxonMobil is one of the Contractors under a Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) covering the Erha block located in the offshore waters of Nigeria. ExxonMobil's affiliate is the operator of the block and owns a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;56.25 percent interest under the PSC. The Contractors are in dispute with NNPC regarding NNPC's lifting of crude oil in excess of its entitlement under the terms of the PSC. In accordance with the terms of the PSC, the Contractors initiated arbitration in Abuja, Nigeria, under the Nigerian Arbitration and Conciliation Act. On October 24, 2011, a three-member arbitral Tribunal issued an award upholding the Contractors' position in all material respects and awarding damages to the Contractors jointly in an amount of approximately $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;1.8 billion plus $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;234 million in accrued interest. The Contractors petitioned a Nigerian federal court for enforcement of the award, and NNPC petitioned the same court to have the award set aside. On May 22, 2012, the court set aside the award. The Contractors appealed that judgment to the Court of Appeal, Abuja Judicial Division. On July 22, 2016, the Court of Appeal upheld the decision of the lower court setting aside the award. On October 21, 2016, the Contractors appealed the decision to the Supreme Court of Nigeria. In June 2013, the Contractors filed a lawsuit against NNPC in the Nigerian federal high court in order to preserve their ability to seek enforcement of the PSC in the courts if necessary. Following dismissal by this court, the Contractors appealed to the Nigerian Court of Appeal in June 2016. In October 2014, the Contractors filed suit in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York (SDNY) to enforce, if necessary, the arbitration award against NNPC assets residing within that jurisdiction. NNPC moved to dismiss the lawsuit. On September 4, 2019, the SDNY dismissed the Contractors&#x2019; petition to recognize and enforce the Erha arbitration award. The Contractors filed a notice of appeal in the Second Circuit on October 2, 2019. At this time, the net impact of this matter on the Corporation's consolidated financial results cannot be reasonably estimated. However, regardless of the outcome of enforcement proceedings, the Corporation does not expect the proceedings to have a material effect upon the Corporation's operations or financial condition.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:LegalMattersAndContingenciesTextBlock>
    <us-gaap:LegalCostsPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2020_TO_Mar31_2020_Entity_0000034088"
      id="ID_570">&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation accrues an undiscounted liability for those contingencies where the incurrence of a loss is probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If a range of amounts can be reasonably estimated and no amount within the range is a better estimate than any other amount, then the minimum of the range is accrued. The Corporation does not record liabilities when the likelihood that the liability has been incurred is probable but the amount cannot be reasonably estimated or when the liability is believed to be only reasonably possible or remote. For contingencies where an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible and which are significant, the Corporation discloses the nature of the contingency and, where feasible, an estimate of the possible loss. For purposes of our contingency disclosures, &#x201c;significant&#x201d; includes material matters, as well as other matters which management believes should be disclosed.&lt;/span&gt;</us-gaap:LegalCostsPolicyTextBlock>

This transaction was not reflected in the consolidated financial statements as of March 31, 2020.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Derivative Instruments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt; The Corporation&#x2019;s size, strong capital structure, geographic diversity and the complementary nature of the Upstream, Downstream and Chemical businesses reduce the Corporation&#x2019;s enterprise-wide risk from changes in commodity prices, currency rates and interest rates. In addition, the Corporation uses commodity-based contracts, including derivatives, to manage commodity price risk and for trading purposes. Commodity contracts held for trading purposes are presented in the Consolidated Statement of Income on a net basis in the line &#x201c;Sales and other operating revenue.&#x201d; The Corporation&#x2019;s commodity derivatives are not accounted for under hedge accounting. At times, the Corporation also enters into currency and interest rate derivatives, none of which are material to the Corporation&#x2019;s financial position as of March 31, 2020, and December 31, 2019, or results of operations for the periods ended March 31, 2020 and 2019.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Credit risk associated with the Corporation&#x2019;s derivative position is mitigated by several factors, including the use of derivative clearing exchanges and the quality of and financial limits placed on derivative counterparties. The Corporation maintains a system of controls that includes the authorization, reporting and monitoring of derivative activity.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;At March 31, 2020, the net notional long/(short) position of derivative instruments was (&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;4) million barrels for crude oil, (&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;36) million barrels for products, and (&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;192) million MMBtus of natural gas.     <us-gaap:AllowanceForCreditLossesTextBlock
      contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2020_TO_Mar31_2020_Entity_0000034088"
      id="ID_d50fcff865004a3799fe00bfe19aed42">&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;10.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="display: inline-block; width: 0.25in;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-weight: bold; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Allowance for Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Effective January 1, 2020, the Corporation adopted the Financial Accounting Standards Board&#x2019;s update, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-style: italic; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;Financial Instruments &#x2013; Credit Losses (Topic 326)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;, as amended. The standard requires a valuation allowance for credit losses be recognized for certain financial assets that reflects the current expected credit loss over the asset&#x2019;s contractual life. The valuation allowance considers the risk of loss, even if remote, and considers past events, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. The standard requires this expected loss methodology for trade receivables, certain other financial assets and off-balance sheet credit exposures. The cumulative effect adjustment related to the adoption of this standard reduced equity by $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;93 million.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation is exposed to credit losses primarily through sales of petroleum products, crude oil, NGLs and natural gas, as well as loans to equity companies and joint venture receivables. A counterparty&#x2019;s ability to pay is assessed through a credit review process that considers payment terms, the counterparty&#x2019;s established credit rating or the Corporation&#x2019;s assessment of the counterparty&#x2019;s credit worthiness, contract terms, country of operation, and other risks. The Corporation can require prepayment or collateral to mitigate certain credit risks.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation groups financial assets into portfolios that share similar risk characteristics for purposes of determining the allowance for credit losses. Each reporting period, the Corporation assesses whether a significant change in the risk of credit loss has occurred. Among the quantitative and qualitative factors considered are historical financial data, current conditions, industry and country risk, current credit ratings and the quality of third-party guarantees secured from the counterparty. Financial assets are written off in whole, or in part, when practical recovery efforts have been exhausted and no reasonable expectation of recovery exists. Subsequent recoveries of amounts previously written off are recognized in earnings. The Corporation manages receivable portfolios using past due balances as a key credit quality indicator. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; line-height: 115.00%; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation recognizes a credit allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures as a liability on the balance sheet, separate from the allowance for credit losses related to recognized financial assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt; Among these exposures are unfunded loans to equity companies and financial guarantees that cannot be cancelled unilaterally by the Corporation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; line-height: 115.00%; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; line-height: 115.00%; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;During the first quarter of 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic spread rapidly through most areas of the world resulting in economic uncertainty, global financial market volatility, and negative effects in the credit markets. The Corporation has considered these effects, along with the significantly lower balances of trade receivables at the end of the quarter, in its estimate of credit losses and concluded no material adjustment to credit allowances in the quarter was required.     <us-gaap:CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FROM_Jan01_2020_TO_Mar31_2020_Entity_0000034088"
      id="ID_39f0f4a4555447bbb5f094cd3705b2b0">&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation groups financial assets into portfolios that share similar risk characteristics for purposes of determining the allowance for credit losses. Each reporting period, the Corporation assesses whether a significant change in the risk of credit loss has occurred. Among the quantitative and qualitative factors considered are historical financial data, current conditions, industry and country risk, current credit ratings and the quality of third-party guarantees secured from the counterparty. Financial assets are written off in whole, or in part, when practical recovery efforts have been exhausted and no reasonable expectation of recovery exists. Subsequent recoveries of amounts previously written off are recognized in earnings. The Corporation manages receivable portfolios using past due balances as a key credit quality indicator. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif'; font-size: 10.00pt"&gt;The Corporation recognizes a credit allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures as a liability on the balance sheet, separate from the allowance for credit losses related to recognized financial assets.&lt;/span&gt;</us-gaap:CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_ExplorationExpense">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Exploration expenses (including prospecting) related to oil and gas producing entities and would be included in operating expenses of that entity. Costs incurred in identifying areas that may warrant examination and in examining specific areas that are considered to have prospects of containing oil and gas reserves, including costs of drilling exploratory wells and exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells. Exploration costs may be incurred both before acquiring the related property (sometimes referred to in part as prospecting costs) and after acquiring the property. Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. Collectively, these are sometimes referred to as geological and geophysical or "G&amp;G" costs. (ii) Costs of carrying and retaining undeveloped properties, such as delay rentals, ad valorem taxes on properties, legal costs for title defense, and the maintenance of land and lease records. (iii) Dry hole contributions and bottom hole contributions. (iv) Costs of drilling and equipping exploratory wells. (v) Costs of drilling exploratory-type stratigraphic test wells.</p></div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for reporting segments including data and tables. Reportable segments include those that meet any of the following quantitative thresholds a) it's reported revenue, including sales to external customers and intersegment sales or transfers is 10 percent or more of the combined revenue, internal and external, of all operating segments b) the absolute amount of its reported profit or loss is 10 percent or more of the greater, in absolute amount of 1) the combined reported profit of all operating segments that did not report a loss or 2) the combined reported loss of all operating segments that did report a loss c) its assets are 10 percent or more of the combined assets of all operating segments.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Amount, excluding tax collected from customer, of revenue from satisfaction of performance obligation by transferring promised good or service to customer. Tax collected from customer is tax assessed by governmental authority that is both imposed on and concurrent with specific revenue-producing transaction, including, but not limited to, sales, use, value added and excise.</p></div>
